issue: Does a conviction for conspiracy (or another inchoate offense) to possess controlled substances with intent to distribute qualify as a 'controlled substance offense' under U.S.S.G. § 4B1.2(b), given that Application Note 1 says it does?

sides.position: Inchoate offenses such as conspiracy and attempt are not 'controlled substance offenses' under § 4B1.2(b); the commentary cannot expand the guideline's unambiguous text.
cases: United States v. Nasir, 17 F.4th 459 (3d Cir. 2021) (en banc)
United States v. Havis, 927 F.3d 382 (6th Cir. 2019) (en banc)
United States v. Winstead, 890 F.3d 1082 (D.C. Cir. 2018)
United States v. Dupree, 57 F.4th 1269 (11th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: Inchoate offenses are included in 'controlled substance offense' under § 4B1.2(b), and Application Note 1 is authoritative and controlling.
cases: United States v. Smith, 989 F.3d 575 (7th Cir.), cert. denied, 142 S. Ct. 488 (2021)
United States v. Lewis, 963 F.3d 16 (1st Cir. 2020)
United States v. Richardson, 958 F.3d 151 (2d Cir. 2020)
United States v. Crum, 934 F.3d 963 (9th Cir. 2019)
United States v. Mendoza-Figueroa, 65 F.3d 691 (8th Cir. 1995) (en banc)

this_court: The Eleventh Circuit holds that inchoate offenses are not controlled substance offenses under § 4B1.2(b), so the enhancement does not apply to Dupree's conspiracy conviction.
quote: Panels of the First, Second, Seventh, and Ninth Circuits, and the Eighth Circuit sitting en banc, have reached the opposite conclusion.
cite: United States v. Brandon Romel Dupree, 57 F. 4th 1269 (11th Cir. 2023)
